criteria.criterion: Run `cargo test --locked -p athena-core reading`: a new test shows a reading with the criterion "the producer's report lists the caller-check Grep" is refused with an error naming that criterion, and the same test fails when the new check is removed.
criteria.evidence: I ran it: 63 passed, including reading::tests::a_criterion_resting_on_the_producers_report_is_refused_and_named. That test calls `unwrap_err()` on `check_criteria_evidence` for exactly this criterion, then checks that the error contains the criterion text, "criterion 1", "a command or Grep the verifier can run" and "file in the snapshot". A check that did nothing would make `unwrap_err` panic. Removing the call from `check_reading_acceptance` would make the_acceptance_check_refuses_a_first_attempt_and_a_retry_alike and the two run_pin_tests fail. I read this from the code; I did not edit the tree to prove it, because my role does not allow edits.

criteria.criterion: Run `cargo test --locked -p athena-core reading`: a test covers each phrase family ("the report lists", "the producer states", "the producer confirms", "producer's summary", "producer's claims") and each is refused.
criteria.evidence: every_phrase_family_that_cites_the_producers_own_account_is_refused passed. It includes "the report lists…", "The producer states…", "the producer confirms…", "the producer’s summary…" (curly apostrophe), "the Producer's claims…", plus a line-break variant and the "according to the producer" and "reported by the producer" forms. Each one must produce an error containing "was refused".

criteria.criterion: Run `cargo test --locked -p athena-core reading`: a test shows criteria naming a command, a Grep, or a file path (e.g. "a Grep of crates/ for `gh::` outside gh/ returns no hits", "cargo test --locked passes") are accepted, so ordinary readings are not refused.
criteria.evidence: criteria_naming_a_command_a_grep_or_a_file_are_accepted passed. It checks 10 ordinary criteria, including both examples from the criterion and near-misses such as "the producer model is on the allowed list" and "the summary section of docs/…". every_refused_criterion_is_named_and_the_others_are_not passed too: in a mixed reading, only the bad criteria are named.

criteria.criterion: Run `cargo test --locked -p athena-core reading`: a test shows the check is wired into the reading path (the reader's output becomes a refusal message, not a Reading) for a first attempt as well as a retry, not only in the check function.
criteria.evidence: run_pin_tests::a_first_reading_resting_on_the_producers_report_comes_back_as_a_refusal_not_a_reading passed. It goes through `Athena::retry` after a rejected job, and the refusal comes from the evidence check, not the previous-result check. Both tests also show a Grep criterion being accepted. findings.summary: A changed file is outside the expected deliverables list
findings.evidence: The expected deliverables are reading.rs, CHANGELOG.md and briefs.rs. The diff also adds 113 lines to run_pin_tests.rs. The addition is test-only and is what proves criterion 4 (the check runs through ask and retry), so it causes no harm, but it is outside the stated scope.

findings.summary: Matching on "the report <verb>" may refuse a legitimate criterion about a report the verifier can generate
findings.evidence: "the report lists", "the report shows" and similar phrases match without the word "producer". So a criterion like "Run `cargo run -- report`: the report lists every job" would be refused, even though the verifier can run that command. The refusal message tells the reader how to restate the criterion, so a retry can recover. It is still a false-positive risk that the tests do not cover.

summary: Pass. The change fixes the cause where it starts: when a reading is accepted. A new check, `check_criteria_evidence`, refuses any acceptance criterion whose evidence is the producer's own report, summary, claims or statement. It runs through `check_reading_acceptance` on every path that builds a reading, first attempt or retry. The refusal names each bad criterion and says to restate it as a command or Grep the verifier can run, or a file in the snapshot. I ran `cargo test --locked -p athena-core reading` and all 63 tests passed. They cover the exact criterion from the failed jobs, every phrase family, ordinary criteria being accepted, and the end-to-end path through `Athena::ask` and `Athena::retry`. The doc comment and the CHANGELOG entry name the root cause and cite all five jobs. Athena's recorded fmt, clippy and full test runs passed. There are two minor findings. First, run_pin_tests.rs is changed but not on the deliverables list; the change is test-only and needed for criterion 4. Second, the bare \"the report lists/shows\" patterns could refuse a criterion about a report the verifier can generate itself.
